events.text: William Dwight Whitney was born in Northampton, Massachusetts.
events.subject: self
events.quote: William Dwight Whitney was born in Northampton , Massachusetts on February 9 , 1827

events.text: Whitney graduated from Williams College.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Whitney entered Williams College at fifteen , graduating in 1845

events.text: Whitney assisted his older brother Josiah Whitney on a geological survey of the Lake Superior region.
events.subject: self
events.object: geological survey of the Lake Superior region
events.quote: assisted his older brother Josiah Whitney on a geological survey of the Lake Superior region in 1849

events.text: Whitney began the study of Sanskrit on the expedition.
events.subject: self
events.quote: On this expedition , he began the study of Sanskrit in his leisure hours

events.text: Whitney left the United States to study philology and Sanskrit in Germany.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1850 , Whitney left the United States to study philology , and especially Sanskrit , in Germany

events.text: Whitney began a major life project, preparation of an edition and translation of the Atharva-veda.
events.subject: self
events.quote: It was during his time in Germany that Whitney began a major life project , preparation of an edition and translation of the Atharva-veda

events.text: Yale University offered Whitney a position as Professor of Sanskrit.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1853 , Yale University offered Whitney a position as Professor of Sanskrit

events.text: Whitney received his doctoral degree from the University of Breslau.
events.subject: self
events.quote: It was not until 1861 , however , that he received his doctoral degree from the University of Breslau

events.text: Whitney served as secretary to the American Oriental Society from 1857.
events.subject: self
events.quote: served as secretary to the American Oriental Society from 1857 until he became its president in 1884

events.text: Whitney served as secretary to the American Oriental Society until 1884.
events.subject: self
events.quote: served as secretary to the American Oriental Society from 1857 until he became its president in 1884

events.text: Whitney became president of the American Oriental Society.
events.subject: self

events.text: The American Philosophical Society elected Whitney to membership.

events.text: Whitney married Elizabeth Wooster Baldwin.
events.subject: self
events.quote: On August 28 , 1856 , Whitney married Elizabeth Wooster Baldwin

events.text: Whitney died at his home, on Whitney Avenue.
events.subject: self
events.quote: He died at his home , on Whitney Avenue , on June 7 , 1894

events.text: Whitney revised definitions for the 1864 edition of Websters American Dictionary.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Whitney revised definitions for the 1864 edition of Websters American Dictionary

events.text: Whitney became a founder and first president of the American Philological Association.
events.subject: self
events.quote: in 1869 became a founder and first president of the American Philological Association

events.text: Whitney also became Yales professor of comparative philology.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In the same year he also became Yales professor of comparative philology

events.text: Whitney's instruction in French and German in the college ended.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Whitney also gave instruction in French and German in the college until 1867

events.text: Whitney's instruction in the Sheffield scientific school ended.
events.subject: self
events.quote: and in the Sheffield scientific school until 1886

events.text: Whitney's papers began to be collected in the Oriental and Linguistic Studies series.
events.subject: part_of_self
events.quote: many of which were collected in the Oriental and Linguistic Studies series ( 1872–74 )

events.text: Whitney's papers finished being collected in the Oriental and Linguistic Studies series.
events.subject: part_of_self
events.quote: many of which were collected in the Oriental and Linguistic Studies series ( 1872–74 )

events.text: His Sanskrit Grammar (1879) contains criticism of the Ashtadhyayi.
events.subject: part_of_self
events.quote: His Sanskrit Grammar ( 1879 ) is notable in part for the criticism it contains of the Ashtadhyayi

events.text: Whitney became editor-in-chief of the first edition of the Century Dictionary.
events.subject: self
events.quote: he was editor-in-chief of the first edition of the respected Century Dictionary , which appeared from 1889 to 1891
